## Root cause

The historical Diffrax snapshot integrates a reverse-oriented interval (`t0 > t1`, as in the supplied study: `1.0 → 0.0`) by flipping to the time variable τ = −t (`_integrate.py`: `direction = jnp.where(t0 < t1, 1, -1)`, then `WrapTerm(term, direction)`). Two things were wrong in that reversal, so the reverse-time ensemble was **not the trajectory ensemble of the model being solved** — it was an O(1)-wrong answer that never improved with step size:

1. **`WrapTerm.contr` negated the whole control, including the space-time Lévy area.** With B(r) = w(s+r(u−s)) − w(s) − r·W_{s,u}, we have H = ∫₀¹B(r)dr and K = ∫₀¹(½−r)B(r)dr. Reversal maps B(r) ↦ B(1−r), so under t ↦ −t: dt ↦ −dt, W ↦ −W, **H ↦ +H (invariant)**, K ↦ −K. Negating H fed every Lévy-area solver (ShARK, SlowRK, SRA1, SPaRK, GeneralShARK, SEA, ALIGN, ShOULD, QUICSORT) an inconsistent control.
2. **`AbstractSRK.step` used `h = t1 - t0` as the drift increment**, which in reversed time is `+|h|`, so the drift was integrated *forwards* while the diffusion went backwards. (`AbstractRungeKutta` and `AbstractFosterLangevinSRK` already take the increment from the term; SRK did not.)
